item.title: Connectivity and control: why militaries relying on Starlink need end-use agreements
item.description: A military that relies on a foreign company for its satellite communications gives up a great degree of control over its own operations. Ukraine, which has relied on Starlink for battlefield communications since the early days of its war with Russia, learned once again in October about the dangers of depending on a foreign capability.

item.description: MANCHESTER, England — China launched a four-satellite technology demonstration mission Wednesday to test key instruments for upcoming flagship space science missions, including a lunar-orbiting radio array.

item.title: France awards $1.7 billion contract for next-generation spy satellites
item.description: JOHANNESBURG — France has awarded Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space a contract worth more than 1.5 billion euros ($1.7 billion) to develop two next-generation military Earth observation satellites.

item.title: Revolv Space closes $5.6 million Series A
item.description: WARSAW, Poland — Revolv Space, an aerospace power system developer based in Italy and the Netherlands, has closed a 5 million euro ($5.6 million) Series A round led by Deep Ocean Capital, aiming to use the funds to bolster research and development as well as production capacities. That brings the company’s fundraising total to 8.6 million euros, 7.8 million of which are in equity, Revolv Space said in a Nov. 11 fundraising announcement.
